{{dropinitial|F|fl={{verse|chapter=25|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Estvs}} therfore vvhen he vvas come into the prouince, after three daies vvent vp to Hieru{{ls}}alem from Cæ{{ls}}aréa. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=2}} And the cheefe prie{{ls}}ts, & principal men of the Iewes vvent vnto him again{{ls}}t Paul: and they de{{ls}}ired him, {{verse|chapter=25|verse=3}} reque{{ls}}ting fauour again{{ls}}t him, that he vvould commaund him to be brought to Hieru{{ls}}alem, laying vvaite for to kil him in the vvay. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=4}} But Fe{{ls}}tus an{{ls}}vvered, that Paul is in Cæ{{ls}}aréa: and that he vvould very {{ls}}hortly goe thither. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=5}} They therfore, {{ls}}aith he, that are of abilitie among you, going dovvne vvith me, if there be any crime in the man, let them accu{{ls}}e him.

{{verse|chapter=25|verse=6}} And hauing taried among them not aboue eight or ten daies, he vvent dovvne to Cæ{{ls}}aréa, and the next day he {{ls}}ate in the iudgement {{ls}}eate: and he commaunded Paul to be brought. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=7}} Vvho being brought, there {{ls}}toode about him the Iewes that vvere come dovvne from Hieru{{ls}}alem, obiecting many and greuous {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''crimes as v. 27''.}}∷ cau{{ls}}es vvhich, they could not proue, {{verse|chapter=25|verse=8}} Paul making an{{ls}}vver, That neither again{{ls}}t the lavv of the Iewes, nor again{{ls}}t the temple, nor again{{ls}}t Cæ{{ls}}ar haue I any thing offended. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=9}} But Fe{{ls}}tus vvilling to {{ls}}hevv the Iewes a plea{{ls}}ure, an{{ls}}vvering Paul, {{ls}}aid, Vvilt thou goe vp to Hieru{{ls}}alem, and there be iudged of the{{ls}}e things before me? {{verse|chapter=25|verse=10}} And Paul {{ls}}aid, At Cæ{{ls}}ars iudgement {{ls}}eate doe I {{ls}}tand, vvhere I ought to be iudged: the Iewes I haue not hurt, as thou very<noinclude>{{continues|vvel}}</noinclude>
